quotes.text: The truth is simpler and harsher. Copilot sees what it's grounded on. Nothing more, nothing less. Out of the box, its field of view is your Microsoft 365 work graph
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one line why default Copilot cannot answer questions about external systems.

quotes.text: If you don't wire an action path to an external system, Copilot can't call it. If you don't expose a knowledge source, Copilot can't cite it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear rule for what an agent needs before it can see or act on enterprise data.

quotes.text: Use studio for fast orchestration and governance. Use toolkit for hard edges, identity and shape. Together the model can't wander. It can only act where you've drawn the map.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the hybrid recommendation of combining Copilot Studio and Teams Toolkit.

quotes.text: If you build in the wrong environment, DLP will silently neuter your agent. Place the agent in an environment classified as business. Put your connectors in the same DLP data group.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical warning about DLP policies blocking agent connectors.

How Copilot sees: knowledge and tools
Path two: Teams Toolkit for VS Code

takeaways: Copilot only sees what it is grounded on, so data in Salesforce, ServiceNow or internal APIs stays invisible until you add knowledge sources and tools with a governed access path.
Copilot Studio gives makers fast, governed orchestration with connectors and citations, while Teams Toolkit gives pro developers strict input validation, minimal response schemas and policy in code.
Licensing, admin approvals, DLP environments, conditional access, least-privilege scopes and logging decide whether an enterprise agent survives beyond the demo.
hook: Microsoft 365 Copilot cannot see your CRM pipeline, your ticket queue or your internal APIs, so it guesses. This episode is for makers, developers and admins who want to build a custom agent grounded in Salesforce, ServiceNow and their own REST API. You learn when to use Copilot Studio, when to use Teams Toolkit, and how to keep identity, DLP and audit under control.
